findings: Exact additive patch structure and baseline preservation: financial-report.patch applies purely additive hunks to docs/CORE-EXECUTION-REPORTS.md (@@ -92,2 +92,37 @@ immediately before '## Provenance and conformance') and openspec/changes/consolidated-language-kernel/specs/consolidated-language-kernel/spec.md (@@ -208,2 +208,4 @@ under UNI-018, @@ -234,2 +236,4 @@ under UNI-020, and @@ -247,2 +251,4 @@ under UNI-021). Every existing baseline line—including NR-01 through NR-06, the five-kind adoption scope, Counter and empty-action specifications, logical-work schedule, public serialization envelopes, and the 28,093-byte mori test normal Transfer compatibility paragraph—is preserved byte-for-byte.

Statement ExprId vs outer typed Step.value representation: Matches crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs (lines 12-52, 146-168, 253-260, 299-322) and crates/mori-core/src/runtime.rs (lines 488-499, 758-861, 902-908). Each completed Transfer, Fee, Liability, and Discharge Step carries its zero-based action ordinal in Step.index (u16, counting preceding nonfinancial statements) and the exact admitted Statement in Step.statement where statement.amount is a numeric zero-based ExprId (u16) indexing Program.expressions. In contrast, outer Step.value is always Some(Value::UInt(q)), serialized via #[serde(tag = "type", content = "value")] and UInt::serialize as {"type":"UInt","value":"<canonical unsigned decimal string>"}, including "0". For Liability and Discharge, Step.value reports the evaluated statement amount q (the added or discharged delta), never the closing duty amount b+q or b-q, recipient balance, ExprId, boolean, or null/omitted.

Effect delta (Step.effects) vs derived prefix (P[i]) and Execution.effects rules: Matches crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs (lines 104-111, 220-251, 262-270) and crates/mori-core/src/runtime.rs (lines 773-787, 827-834, 852-859, 885-917). Step.effects contains only the single newly produced effect for that financial statement (not an accumulated prefix): Effect::Transfer { asset: A, from, to, amount: q }, Effect::Fee { asset: A, from, to, amount: q }, or Effect::Liability { name, asset, debtor, creditor, before, after }. Discharge reuses the Effect::Liability variant (with before: b and after: b-q, and asset/debtor/creditor cloned from the existing liability row) rather than introducing a Discharge effect variant. Within Effect, asset is the full resolved AssetId { network, issuer, reference, scale } rather than the Statement asset alias string, and amount/before/after serialize as bare canonical decimal strings (UInt) without a typed Value wrapper. P[-1]=[] and P[i]=P[i-1] ++ Step[i].effects remain derived notation (not wire fields), and Execution.effects is the ordered concatenation of all Step.effects across the action, including intervening nonfinancial effects (State, Emit), preserving duplicates and order.

Zero-amount and self-movement effects plus absent vs present-zero duty distinctions: Matches crates/mori-core/src/runtime.rs (lines 433-444, 612-669, 671-703, 790-861). In move_funds (lines 671-703), self-transfer and self-fee (f == t) still verify account existence and sufficient balance (checked_sub) and leave numeric balances unchanged while execute_statement still pushes the explicit Effect::Transfer or Effect::Fee delta. Zero-amount (q == 0) Transfer and Fee statements likewise emit their explicit effect with amount "0" while balances remain unchanged. For Liability with q == 0 when the named duty is absent in S[i-1], runtime.rs (lines 806-826) inserts a new Liability row with amount UInt(0) sorted by name and emits Effect::Liability { before: "0", after: "0" }; when already present with amount b == 0, it retains the row and emits the same Effect::Liability { before: "0", after: "0" }. For Discharge (lines 837-860), full discharge (q == b) or zero discharge (q == 0) mutates l.amount = after in place and retains the zero-amount duty row in Snapshot.liabilities. Because Expr::LiabilityPresent checks row.is_some() (line 440) while Expr::LiabilityAmount returns row.map_or(UInt(0), |l| l.amount) (line 442), absent duties and present-zero duties remain observationally and semantically distinct in snapshots, and an Effect::Liability with before: "0" requires S[i-1] (and Step.statement) to distinguish absent creation from present-zero addition or zero discharge.

Complete post-statement Snapshot frame and canonical ordering: Matches crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs (lines 188-218) and crates/mori-core/src/runtime.rs (lines 531-670, 817-826, 881-917). Each Step.snapshot equals S[i] in full with exact fields state, balances, and liabilities. Snapshot.state retains all declared states and excludes action inputs and let captures (which live only in env). Balances retain { account, asset, amount } ordered by (asset, account) where AssetId orders by (network, issuer, reference, scale). Liabilities retain { name, asset, debtor, creditor, amount } ordered by name. Untouched observer balances and incoming external duties admitted by scenario_snapshot remain preserved across all steps. Empty state is {} and empty balance/liability vectors are []. For N>0, Execution.post equals the last Step.snapshot; for N=0, pre == post, steps: [], and effects: [] with no synthetic Step. Logical-work charging (charge_logical in runtime.rs lines 411-431, 713) and public envelope shapes remain unchanged with no per-Step work field.

Preservation of missing Mint/Burn/Accrual obligations, non-inference of test/consumer coverage, and governance/security boundaries: Matches crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs (lines 120-169, 278-322), crates/mori-core/src/parser.rs (lines 330-362), crates/mori-core/tests/financial_pair.rs (lines 107-155), and crates/mori/tests/core_test_report.rs (lines 107-179). Core/1 has no Mint, Burn, or dedicated accrual statements; Statement::Liability performs only explicit UInt creation/addition without interest rate, time basis, day-count, compounding, or accrual schedule. Mint/burn and dedicated accrual obligations remain open where required by the broader product. Existing financial_pair.rs checks pre, post, effects, step.index, step.statement.kind, step.snapshot, and step.effects, but omits full raw step.statement (asset/party strings and amount ExprId) and step.value; core_test_report.rs pins the 28,093-byte mori test aggregate report rather than ordinary mori simulate bytes. All U0-U7, M1-M17, MC/SP/G, ACTUS/DeFi, and composition exits remain open, permissionless public developer use (UNI-001) is untouched, and all conservation, authorization, soundness, proof, and hostile-test judgments remain with the designated security owner.

Required adoption-status transition note and concrete wording revisions upon formal adoption: The exact candidate financial-report.patch is technically accurate and suitable for adoption as an unadopted candidate specification. However, because the patch text explicitly labels itself unadopted in headings and normative sentences, applying financial-report.patch verbatim does not by itself make its SHALL clauses the active contract until an explicit adoption decision is recorded. When recording formal adoption (after the required two independent reviewer votes), either record an explicit adoption receipt binding this section or apply the concrete wording transition revisions: (1) in docs/CORE-EXECUTION-REPORTS.md, change '## Proposed financial observation extension (unadopted)' to '## Financial observation extension (NR-07–09)' (or '## Adopted financial observation extension'), replace 'This section is a proposed additive observation contract... Its SHALL clauses remain unadopted until a separately recorded design decision.' with 'This section defines the adopted additive observation contract for normally accepted finite Rust `moriarty/1` / `moriarty-core/1` Transfer, Fee, Liability and Discharge statements, adopted by recorded design decision on 2026-10-18.', and optionally clarify in the first table introduction that 'Let A be the exact declared AssetId denoted by its asset alias (or, for Discharge, the existing duty row''s AssetId in S[i-1]).'; (2) in openspec/changes/consolidated-language-kernel/specs/consolidated-language-kernel/spec.md under UNI-018, UNI-020, and UNI-021, replace the three '**Proposed financial ... (unadopted).**' lead-ins, anchor link '#proposed-financial-observation-extension-unadopted', and 'remain unadopted until a separately recorded design decision' / 'SHALL remain design-only until independently adopted' phrases with adopted labels referencing the recorded decision while keeping implementation, independent expectation freezes, and runtime conformance separate.
limitations: Review is strictly a static, read-only design and source-correspondence audit of the pinned files in /home/charl/moriarty-c2-opus55-restored-20261017/financial-report-design-review-packet; no commands, toolchain, compiler, Cargo test, Mori runtime, SDK, prover, or network operations were executed.

The proposal author was exposed to current implementation source (crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs, parser.rs, runtime.rs, README.md) and this reviewer likewise inspected those pinned baseline sources; source-to-design agreement does not constitute independent runtime behavior evidence, compiler/lowering correspondence, or independently derived test goldens.

Existing crates/mori-core/tests/financial_pair.rs does not assert full raw Step.statement members (asset/account/party strings or amount ExprId) or outer Step.value, and crates/mori/tests/core_test_report.rs covers the mori test aggregate consumer for a single Transfer case rather than ordinary mori simulate byte envelopes or Fee/Liability/Discharge raw steps; independent expectations must be derived and frozen separately before conformance runs.

The patch text itself contains explicit '(unadopted)' headings and self-limiting clauses ('remain unadopted until a separately recorded design decision'); therefore, adopting the design requires either an explicit recorded adoption decision referencing the candidate or a follow-up wording promotion removing the unadopted qualifiers once both independent review votes are recorded.

Per role scope, this review makes no judgment on asset conservation, authorization, authentication, circuit/witness soundness, cryptographic proofs, or hostile/security test coverage, which remain with the designated security owner, and closes no U0-U7, M1-M17, or MC/SP/G exit.
summary: ADOPT (adopt-design) for exact additive candidate financial-report.patch. Independent inspection against the pinned DTO, parser, runtime, test, and specification baselines confirms that the patch accurately and completely specifies the observational report contract for accepted finite Core/1 Transfer, Fee, Liability, and Discharge statements without altering financial admission or arithmetic, inventing Mint/Burn/Accrual semantics, waiving any U0-U7/M1-M17/MC/SP/G obligation, inferring unrun full-Step or consumer-byte coverage, encroaching on security-owner scope, or gating permissionless public developers. Because the patch text is explicitly written as an unadopted candidate ('(unadopted)' headings and clauses deferring effect until a separately recorded design decision), formal activation as the effective contract requires an explicit recorded adoption decision (and, when promoting the text from candidate to adopted status, the concrete wording revisions detailed in the findings).
